$comment: Golden targets for the VMOS Edge fleet. check-drift.mjs compares every live box against these values. The proxy version is NOT recorded here: it is read from infra/magicbox-proxy/package.json (the code IS the source of truth).
captured_from: GET /v1/get_hardware_cfg on every live box. Prefer it over /v1/systeminfo: it reports `model`, `version` (CBS) and `kernel_version` on ALL boxes, whereas /v1/systeminfo leaves cbs/kernel blank on the 1.1.4.x CBS line (box-2/3/4).

android_image.$comment: Model-independent — the Android image runs on any host model. New devices MUST be created on it so they are born fleet-aligned: pass it to MagicBox-Industrial as --image-repository <golden> (it defaults to VMOS's ancient built-in image otherwise). This file is the single source of truth for the value; do not re-hardcode it in the provisioning repo.
android_image.distribution: No export endpoint exists in the Container API (only POST /v1/import_image, an upload). Moving it to another box means `docker save` on box-5 and `docker load` on the target, over SSH — roughly 3.4 GB per box. Do not attempt it without a justification stronger than uniformity.

vendor_by_model.$comment: The fleet spans TWO hardware models that do NOT share a kernel: box-1..4 are `L1`, box-5 is `E1.01`. Converging an L1 onto the E1.01 kernel through POST /v1/update_kernel would flash firmware from the wrong family. Each model therefore carries its own baseline, set to the highest version actually observed on that model — which is why the L1 target is a composite: box-1 leads on CBS (1.1.6.12.1) while box-2/3/4 lead on kernel (2.0.30_marsbox). No single L1 box is yet on target.

vendor_upgrade_path.$comment: The vendor layer IS upgradable through the official API — an earlier revision of this file wrongly claimed it was not shippable and pointed at a scripts/deploy-vendor.sh that never existed.
vendor_upgrade_path.cbs: POST /v1/update_cbs (multipart, file named cbs_go_edge_<version>, optional .cbs suffix)
vendor_upgrade_path.constraint: Match the hardware model. Read `model` from /v1/get_hardware_cfg before pushing anything.

host_disk.$comment: Disk headroom is a production gate, not a nicety. box-1 reached 98% on /container_nswc_lv in June 2026: guest ext4 writes began failing with EIO (superblock: ext4_check_bdev_write_error, 13 Jun 2026), 44 of its 96 containers took the filesystem error flag, and its job success rate sat at 31% against 70% on a healthy box. Container data.img files are sparse and grow-only — the loop devices are not mounted with discard — so allocation never shrinks on its own.
host_disk.reclaim: Offline maintenance pass: e2fsck -fy, purge /tombstones + /anr + /local/tmp/scd.log, then mount -o loop,discard and fstrim. Recovered 129 GB across 95 containers on box-1 (98% → 69%) with identity and app data untouched.

reference_capacity.$comment: Fleet policy (2026-07-07): max_concurrent_containers = 10 on every box — the VMOS host ceiling (AGENTS.md). Proven on box-5 at 16 GB RAM; box-2/3/4 have the same 16 GB and box-1 has 32 GB, so 10 is safe fleet-wide. operator_reserve stays 1 (the automator uses max-1). check-drift flags divergence from this value.

control_api_minimums.$comment: Floor required by the Android Control API v2 (input/click, accessibility/dump, node find-and-act). Source: help.vmosedge.com/en/sdk/agent-api. The whole fleet already exceeds these. Note that the v2 AGENT version tracks the Android image, not the host CBS: images 20260417 carry agent 1.1.1, images 20260511 and 20260626 carry 1.1.3 (131 vs 137 endpoints, strictly additive).
